name: SEC Form D filings (EDGAR)
covers: New fund vehicle closes, fund sizes, entity names. The primary source for fund vintage and capacity.
notes: The single best free source for 'have they just raised a new fund'. Search the management company name.

name: SEC Form ADV / IAPD
covers: Registered adviser AUM, ownership, control persons.
notes: Useful for larger firms. Many early-stage funds are exempt reporting advisers with thinner filings.

name: Firm website and portfolio pages
covers: Stated thesis, current portfolio, partner roster, contact route.
notes: The authoritative source for portfolio and partner lists. Always the first check for a conflict.

name: Firm published theses and memos
covers: What they say they are looking for, in their own words.
notes: Read before the first call. Quote it back to them.

name: Crunchbase
covers: Deal history, co-investors, round sizes, investor pace.
notes: Good for pace and co-investor graphs; coverage of small rounds is patchy.

name: PitchBook
covers: Fund vintages, dry powder estimates, deal terms, partner deal attribution.
notes: The most complete paid option. Worth a trial during an active raise.

name: Dealroom
covers: Deal and fund data with reasonable non-US coverage.
notes: Useful for the India-corridor funds where US databases are thin.

name: Tracxn
covers: India and cross-border fund and deal coverage.
notes: Better than most US databases for India-based funds.

name: Signal by NFX
covers: Partner-level stage and sector focus, warm-intro path discovery.
notes: Fastest way to find which partner at a firm owns a thesis.

name: OpenVC
covers: Cheque sizes, stage, geography and whether a fund is open to cold inbound.
notes: Self-reported by funds - treat cheque ranges as indicative.

name: TechCrunch
covers: Fund closes, financings, personnel moves.
notes: Good for the 'In the News' feed. Confirm figures against filings.

name: Axios Pro Rata
covers: Daily venture deal and fund news.
notes: Efficient daily scan for fund closes and partner moves.

name: StrictlyVC
covers: Fund news and investor interviews.

name: The Information
covers: Fund performance, LP sentiment, partner departures ahead of the wire.
notes: Often the earliest signal that a firm is in trouble or between funds.

name: LinkedIn
covers: Partner hires and departures, title changes, shared connections for intros.
notes: The most reliable early signal on personnel changes. Also the practical warm-intro finder.

name: Founder and investor networks on X
covers: Stated theses, live commentary, who is actively deploying.
notes: Directional only. Never a citation.

name: AlphaSense / Tegus
covers: Expert call transcripts and research synthesis on the categories investors will diligence.
notes: Investors may run expert diligence on us. Knowing what the corpus already says is worth the subscription during a raise.

name: Third Bridge
covers: Analyst-led interviews and transcript library covering restaurant, delivery and ad-platform ecosystems.
notes: Publishes research directly adjacent to the platform-risk objection.

name: GLG
covers: Custom expert calls, pricing and willingness-to-pay research.
notes: The route to independent willingness-to-pay evidence.

name: Guidepoint
covers: Expert transcripts and rapid customer and competitor reference checks.

name: NewtonX
covers: Verified B2B quantitative panels - TAM, buyer demand and willingness to pay.
notes: Best source for independent quantitative proof of buyer demand.

name: References from their portfolio founders
covers: How the firm actually behaves after the wire: support, follow-on, board conduct.
notes: The highest-value source and the one most founders skip. Ask for two names they did not offer.

name: LP and fund-of-funds contacts
covers: Whether a fund is actually deploying, and its remaining reserves.
notes: Hard to access but decisive on timing.
